Facts: the ball touched the striker's bat, did not touch the ground before control was complete, the boundary came directly from the delivery and not from an overthrow, the agreed boundary allowance was 4 runs, the fielding side appealed before the next run-up and before Time was called, and the fielder ultimately controlled both ball and movement with no boundary contact before control was complete. Laws 33.1-33.3 (Caught) are satisfied, but the wicket event was submitted as Caught without a dismissal ordinal or identified dismissed batter in this incident's evidence, so no dismissal is recorded. Scoring: 4 batter runs from the bat; legal delivery counting in the over; no extras. Counterfactual (single change: the fielder touched the boundary while carrying the ball before completing control): under Laws 33.1-33.3 boundary grounding before completion prevents a fair catch, so the Catch fails; the ball remains live and in play, so the pre-wicket ball state stays DEAD only in the sense that the delivery is complete with the boundary scored; the 4 runs remain credited to the batter as the agreed boundary allowance struck by the bat, with no dismissal and no change to the run ledger.

Source selection: the signed match-control procedure fixes the review lock at 18:25 and requires the latest signed entry at or before the lock for the same observation, so active_source is LAST_PRE_LOCK; the later-locked worksheet entry stating the wicket was put down fairly belongs to the next reconciliation cycle, and the latest pre-lock entry records that the wicket was not put down fairly. Facts: the ball touched the striker's bat, 1 completed run preceded the terminal event, the wicket event was submitted as Run out, the fielding side appealed, the ball was still in play when the wicket was broken, and the loose ball reached the boundary only after the wicket event. Laws 38.1-38.2 (Run out) are satisfied and Laws 20.1/20.6 confirm the later boundary contact cannot score, so the boundary allowance is 0 and the ball was dead for scoring after the wicket. Counterfactual (single change: the wicket was fairly put down): the Run out fails and the dismissal becomes NONE; the wicket is never broken so the ball stays LIVE; the 1 completed run is retained and the post-wicket boundary is not scored because the delivery is complete with the run scored; all other facts and source selections are preserved.

However, Laws 31.1/31.3 require the fielding side to appeal for the specific dismissal sought; the dossier records only a generic fielding-side appeal with no appeal for Stumped or Run out, so no dismissal can be recorded and the not-out decision stands. Scoring: legal delivery, no contact, no completed runs, no extras; total 0 and the delivery counts in the over. Counterfactual (single change: No-ball signalled): the delivery becomes NO_BALL and does not count in the over; Law 21.17 makes Stumped unavailable and Law 38.2.2.2 bars Run out because the wicket-keeper alone put down the wicket with the striker not attempting a run, so the batter remains not out; with no contact and no completed runs the only score would be the No-ball extra, but the dossier records no completed runs or penalty for this delivery, so the recorded total remains 0 with the delivery status changed.
